detail.longDescription: I have a very long non-paginated (deliberate) tabulator table designed to create a quotation price list. I don't want a scrollbar inside the table, so I have set the height to 100%. The main table holds the categories and under each category is a nested table using a custom rowformatter that holds the items and their pricing details. On each row of the main table i have a button that adds a new row to its related sub-table. When you click add on a row part way down the page, it automatically scrolls back to the top of the page, as opposed to keeping the new row in view. If i set the table to a smaller size, say 500px, it works as intended however you have the scrollbar which I do not want. tl;dr Is there anyway to prevent the automated scroll back to the top of the page when you add a row programmatically to a sub-table that is part way down the page? An example is below and can be tested in this jsfiddle var rowTools = function (cell, formatterParams, onRendered){ var button = document.createElement("button"); button.textContent = "Add Item"; button.addEventListener("click", function (event) { event.preventDefault(); // Prevent the default button behavior cell.getRow().getData().subTable.addData({ item: "New Item" }, false); }); return button; }; var columns = [ { title: "Category", field: "heading", editor:"input", editorParams:{search:true}, validator:"required" }, { title:"", field: "", formatter: rowTools, formatterParams:{} } ]; var table = new Tabulator("#pricingGrid", { height:"100%", columns: columns, placeholder: "No Data Available", rowFormatter:function(row){ //create and style holder elements var holderEl = document.createElement("div"); var tableEl = document.createElement("div"); holderEl.appendChild(tableEl); row.getElement().appendChild(holderEl); var subTable = new Tabulator(tableEl, { rowHeader: { headerSort: false, }, height:"100%", data:row.getData().items, columns:[ { title: "Item", field: "item"} ] }); row.getData().subTable = subTable; // Store the sub-table instance in the row data for later access) }, }); var data = fetch("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thedigitaltailor/store/cb842c6d73ffaec1b7e3a0aa74cde31088c30041/sample.json") .then(response => { if (!response.ok) { throw new Error('Network response was not ok'); } return response.json(); }) .then(data => { table.setData(data); // Process your JSON data here }) .catch(error => { console.error('Error loading JSON from GitHub:', error); });
